questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A radioactive half-life is the time required for the number of undecayed nuclei to fall to:
questions.explanation: After one half-life, on average half the original radioactive nuclei remain undecayed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The number of protons in a nucleus is called the:
questions.explanation: Atomic number Z equals the number of protons.

questions.explanation: Ohmâs law gives I = V/R = 12 V / 6 Î© = 2 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For a resistor, electrical power can be written as:
questions.explanation: Electrical power equals voltage multiplied by current; equivalent forms include IÂ²R and VÂ²/R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Resistors connected in series have an equivalent resistance equal to:
questions.optionD: The product divided by the sum always
questions.explanation: Series resistances add because the same current passes through each resistor.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The equivalent resistance of two equal resistors R connected in parallel is:
questions.explanation: For two equal resistors in parallel, 1/Req = 1/R + 1/R, so Req = R/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is:
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors, 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Faraday's law relates induced emf to the rate of change of:
questions.explanation: The magnitude of induced emf is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Coulomb's law states that electrostatic force magnitude varies inversely with:
questions.optionA: Separation distance to the fourth power
questions.optionC: Mass of a test charge only
questions.explanation: For point charges, Coulomb force is proportional to the product of charges and inversely proportional to r squared.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The SI unit of electric potential difference is:
questions.explanation: Potential difference is measured in volts, equivalent to joules per coulomb.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The electric field direction is defined as the direction of force on a:
questions.explanation: By convention, electric field points in the direction a positive test charge would be pushed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The electric potential due to a point charge q at distance r in vacuum is:
questions.explanation: Electric potential of a point charge is V = kq/r; kq/r² is the magnitude of electric field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: If the distance between two point masses is doubled, the gravitational force becomes:
questions.explanation: Newtonâs law gives F â 1/rÂ²; doubling r changes the force by 1/2Â² = 1/4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The gravitational force between two point masses follows an inverse-square dependence on:
questions.explanation: Newton's law gives gravitational force proportional to 1/rÂ².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A net force of 10 N acts on a 2 kg object. Its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Newtonâs second law gives a = F/m = 10 N / 2 kg = 5 m sâ»Â².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The SI unit of magnetic field is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux density is measured in tesla.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The energy of a photon is given by:
questions.explanation: Photon energy equals Planck's constant multiplied by frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The photoelectric effect supports the idea that light energy is exchanged in:
questions.explanation: The photoelectric effect is explained by photons transferring discrete energy hÎ½ to electrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For constant acceleration, the equation v = u + at relates final velocity to:
questions.explanation: The kinematic equation gives final velocity v from initial velocity u, acceleration a and time t.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The slope of a displacement-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: The gradient of displacement with respect to time is velocity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m sâ»Â² for 3 s. Its final speed is:
questions.explanation: Using v = u + at with u = 0, a = 2 m sâ»Â² and t = 3 s gives v = 6 m sâ»Â¹.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Newton's third law states that action and reaction forces are:
questions.optionA: Unequal and on the same body
questions.optionC: Always parallel in the same direction
questions.optionD: Equal in magnitude and opposite in direction on different bodies
questions.explanation: Action-reaction forces are equal, opposite and act on different interacting bodies.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A convex lens for an object beyond its focal length can form a real image that is:
questions.explanation: For a converging lens with the object outside the focal length, the image is real and inverted.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For a spherical mirror, the focal length magnitude is half the radius of curvature magnitude. This relation is:
questions.explanation: For a spherical mirror under the paraxial approximation, the focal length is half the radius of curvature; signs depend on the sign convention.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The refractive index of a medium is the ratio of light speed in vacuum to:
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = c/v, where c is vacuum light speed and v is speed in the medium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In simple harmonic motion, restoring acceleration is:
questions.optionC: Proportional to displacement and directed toward equilibrium
questions.explanation: For SHM, a = âÏÂ²x, directed opposite to displacement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Pressure is defined as:
questions.explanation: Pressure equals the normal force divided by the area over which it acts.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The SI unit of density is:
questions.explanation: Density is mass per volume, so its SI unit is kilogram per cubic metre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A pure semiconductor at room temperature has:
questions.optionC: Electrons and holes as charge carriers
questions.explanation: Thermal excitation creates mobile electrons and corresponding holes in an intrinsic semiconductor.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Sound waves in air are primarily:
questions.explanation: Air sound propagates through compressions and rarefactions parallel to the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: During melting of a pure substance at its melting point, supplied heat primarily increases:
questions.optionB: Potential energy during the phase change
questions.explanation: Latent heat changes phase by altering intermolecular potential energy while temperature remains constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For an ideal gas, the equation of state is:
questions.explanation: The ideal gas law relates pressure, volume, amount of gas and absolute temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the change in internal energy is:
questions.optionB: Equal to the work in all sign conventions
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature. An isothermal process has ÎT = 0, so ÎU = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The first law of thermodynamics expresses conservation of:
questions.explanation: The first law relates heat, internal-energy change and work, expressing energy conservation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The SI base unit of electric current is:
questions.explanation: Ampere is the SI base unit for electric current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The SI unit of energy is:
questions.explanation: Energy and work are measured in joules.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The dimensional formula of force is:
questions.explanation: From F = ma, dimensions are mass Ã length/timeÂ², giving [M L Tâ»Â²].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The dimensional formula of velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity is displacement divided by time, giving dimension length per time.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For a wave of fixed speed, if frequency doubles, its wavelength becomes:
questions.explanation: Since v = fÎ» and speed is fixed, doubling frequency halves wavelength.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The wave speed is equal to frequency multiplied by:
questions.explanation: Wave speed v equals frequency f times wavelength Î».

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A 2 kg object moving at 3 m s⁻¹ has kinetic energy:
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is ½mv² = ½×2×3² = 9 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Kinetic energy of a body of mass m and speed v is:
questions.explanation: Translational kinetic energy is one-half mass times speed squared.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The SI unit of power is:
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work and is measured in watts.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The work done by a constant force perpendicular to the displacement is:
questions.explanation: Work W = Fs cos Î¸. At Î¸ = 90Â°, cos Î¸ = 0, so the work is zero.
